verdicts.reason: True in the current repo: F-6-2 is reached only from NONE and F-6-1, while 37 long-term statuses offer F-6-1. The 2026.9.18 manual documents a change to F-6-2 for 'a parent on a status other than F-6', so the missing edges are real. The F-6-1 half of the claim is overstated: in simulation F-6-1 -> F-6-2 is OPEN for readers who answered divorced/widowed or not married, and BLOCKED only for 'married to a Korean' and, since F-6-1 gained `gives: {spouse: korean}` after this finding, for readers who left marital status blank. The proposed move-level `needs: {koreanChild: true}` would show F-6-2 as open to readers still married to a Korean, who belong on F-6-1, so the new edges should be bare and the blank-reader problem should be fixed by removing the gives.

verdicts.reason: Confirmed in the repo: F-3 how.en reads 'Spouse or minor child of a D, E or F-2 status holder.' The visa manual transcribed in visadocs lists the sponsors as D-1, D-2, D-4–E-7, F-2, F-4 or H-2, and separate F-3-19/F-3-20 cases cover F-4/H-2 family. The extra claim that F-2 '타목' (family categories) is excluded could not be checked against the decree this session. The engine cannot gate on the sponsor's status, so a text fix is the right remedy, but it should leave out the unverified F-2 exception.

verdicts.reason: The how text is wrong. 나목 of the decree has no 'marriage ended' element and includes de facto relationships. The manual's own lists ask for proof that the marriage ended only '해당자에 한함' and have a separate document for a child born in a 사실혼. So 'After the marriage ... ended' misdescribes never-married parents. The needs half of the claim is wrong: `spouse: [exKorean, none]` already admits never-married parents ('none'). Dropping the spouse condition, as proposed, would show F-6-2 to readers legally married to a Korean, who use F-6-1. Only 'korean' should be excluded, which also admits a parent who has since married someone else. The proposed sentence 'Open from any status other than F-6' is also misleading: F-6-1 holders reach F-6-2 by an extension, and a consular visa exists too.

The finding's premise that 'the edge itself is fine' is also wrong. The F-2-99 eligible-status list (신청 대상 체류자격) contains no 동반(F-3), and the repo's own statusGroups.longTerm used by F-2-99's stay check leaves F-3 out. verdicts.reason: In the repo, F-4-R's next is only [F-5-6R]. F-5-6R has no manual entry at all (see f5#12). The decree's F-5-6 ground is time on the 재외동포(F-4) status, and F-4-R is a sub-code of that status: visadocs records F-4>F-4-R and F-4-R>F-4 as within-status changes, and the F-4-R change uses the F-4 integrated application form. The fix is expressible. F-4-R>F-4 has a within rule (use: change), F-5-6 has a change list, and F-5-6's `stay: {years: 2, in: [F-4]}` already counts F-4-R years because isStatus treats F-4-R as F-4. Simulation shows F-5-6R, F-5-6 and F-4 all open from F-4-R. Caveat: no text names F-4-R in the F-5-6 rule, so 'F-4-R years count' rests on the status definition.

verdicts.reason: Right that F-1 offers no F-2-99 while F-3 does, and that 방문동거(F-1) is on the F-2-99 eligible-status list (the repo's statusGroups.longTerm includes F-1 too). Wrong that the rule counts 'any long-term status other than A-1 to A-3': the manual narrows the decree to a closed list without F-3. So the consistent fix is the finding's alternative, dropping F-3 -> F-2-99. A lead that restates the manual limits the F-1 route to Korea-born Taiwanese Chinese (화교), and F-2-99 requires current economic activity, which F-1 rarely allows. The repo's KIIP exemption for Korea-born Taiwanese Chinese also fits this. A broad F-1 -> F-2-99 edge with the proposed generic note would therefore mislead most F-1 holders; if added, it should be gated to TW.

verdicts.reason: True that nothing leads to F-1 and F-6-1 has no F-1 move. The 2026.9.18 manual documents '가사정리(F-1-6) 체류기간 연장허가' inside the F-6 chapter (and in the F-1 chapter), and the Visa Navigator says a 혼인단절 spouse who does not qualify as F-6 may change to F-1. Three corrections. (1) F-1 has only an `extend` list, so an in-Korea F-6-1 -> F-1 edge fails the test 'a move inside Korea goes to a visa the manual lets you change to there' unless a rule is added. It also shows no list on the docs page, whose makeMove honours `within` rules only for same-status moves. (2) The edge must be gated `spouse: exKorean` like F-6-3, or still-married readers see it. (3) The F-6-3 -> F-1 edge is unsupported, since F-1-6 is for those who do NOT qualify for F-6-3. Minor: the claim that F-6-3 is always blocked is wrong; it is open for an 'ex-Korean spouse' reader.

verdicts.reason: Correct: F-4 how.en says 'former Korean citizen or descendant'. The decree defines 외국국적동포 by nationality held BY BIRTH, which the repo's manual-derived visadocs also uses ('Former Korean national by birth ... (F-4-41)'). However, the proposed text drops the decree's parenthetical that includes Koreans who emigrated before the 1948 government. Those are exactly the Koryo-saram who make up much of this site's Uzbek and Russian audience, and the new wording 'held Korean nationality by birth' could make them think they do not qualify. Keep that group explicit. The military-service sentence is right and should stay.
